flaws.locator: Theorem 1.6 = Theorem 3.1 (label maint), proof (Section 3): Lemma 3.4's claim 'We know already that D_0 = {(A, s^A) in F : s^A is the antidiagonal of A} is coinitial in F (Lemma 2.12)' and, through Proposition 2.5 (the JPP, used by Proposition 3.3), the step 'Without loss of generality, s^A and s^B are antidiagonals': Lemma 2.12 (label slawek) is applied to structures of v1's class F whose relation s^A need not be symmetric, while the epimorphic image of an antidiagonal is symmetric; v2 adds 'symmetric' to the lemma's hypotheses and restricts the class to involutions
